Aṭāna.arohana: S R2 M1 P N3 S
Aṭāna.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 P G3 R2 S
Aṭāna.description: Majestic, martial-flavoured raga full of powerful gamakas; its jagged descent and bold nishada give it instant dramatic presence.

Behāg.arohana: S G3 M1 P N3 D2 N3 S
Behāg.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M2 G3 M1 G3 R2 S
Behāg.description: A sweet Hindustani import that uses both madhyamas; a favourite for tillānas, padams and film-song adaptations, which make up most of what is sung in it.

Bhairavi.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2 S
Bhairavi.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
Bhairavi.description: One of the grandest and oldest ragas of the tradition, distinguished by its two dhaivatas; a concert mainstay for elaborate alapana and niraval.

Bilahari.arohana: S R2 G3 P D2 S
Bilahari.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Bilahari.description: Bright, energetic morning raga — pentatonic on the way up, full on the way down; radiates optimism.

Bēgaḍa.arohana: S G3 R2 G3 M1 P D2 P S
Bēgaḍa.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Bēgaḍa.description: A connoisseur's raga of sliding, zig-zag phrases; its softened nishada and curling gamakas defy plain scale description.

Dhanyāsi.arohana: S G2 M1 P N2 S
Dhanyāsi.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R1 S
Dhanyāsi.description: Poignant, devotional morning raga — pentatonic ascent opening into a full todi-family descent.

Dēvagāndhāri.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
Dēvagāndhāri.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Dēvagāndhāri.description: Slow, dignified and heavily ornamented; close to Arabhi on paper but unmistakable in its unhurried gait.

Gauḷa.arohana: S R1 M1 P N3 S
Gauḷa.avarohana: S N3 P M1 R1 G3 M1 R1 S
Gauḷa.description: One of the five ghana ragas — ancient, austere and rhythmic, with a signature sharp ri-ga twist in descent.

Harikāmbhōji.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
Harikāmbhōji.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Harikāmbhōji.description: The sunny parent scale of a huge janya family (Kambhoji, Mohanam, Khamas...); warm and open in character.

Hussēnī.melakarta: janya of 22 Karaharapriya (with anya svara shades)
Hussēnī.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P N2 D2 N2 S
Hussēnī.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
Hussēnī.description: A tender, pathos-laden raga beloved of padam composers; its shading of the dhaivata gives it a distinctive ache.

Kalyāṇi.arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N3 S
Kalyāṇi.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M2 G3 R2 S
Kalyāṇi.description: The queen of the prati-madhyama ragas — regal, radiant and inexhaustible; a pillar of every concert repertoire.

Kamās.arohana: S M1 G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
Kamās.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Kamās.description: Lilting and romantic, launched from its characteristic sa-ma leap; equally at home in kritis, javalis and light pieces.

Karaharapriya.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2 S
Karaharapriya.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
Karaharapriya.description: A vast, even-toned parent raga that rewards long alapanas; Tyāgarāja's kritis made it a concert heavyweight.

Kāmavardani.arohana: S R1 G3 M2 P D1 N3 S
Kāmavardani.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M2 G3 R1 S
Kāmavardani.description: Intense and austere with sharpened madhyama against flattened ri-dha; carries a serious, penitential mood.

Kānaḍa.arohana: S R2 P G2 M1 D2 N2 S
Kānaḍa.avarohana: S N2 P M1 G2 M1 R2 S
Kānaḍa.description: A vakra beauty defined by its curling ga-ma phrases rather than any straight scale; instantly recognizable, endlessly subtle.

Kāpi.arohana: S R2 M1 P N3 S
Kāpi.avarohana: S N2 D2 N2 P M1 G2 R2 S (anya svara G3)
Kāpi.description: A folk-tinged, emotive raga that freely borrows foreign notes; the sound of lullabies, bhajans and tear-jerking film songs. The kākali niṣāda in the ascent is what separates it from Karnataka Kāpi, a different raga that takes the kaiśiki niṣāda there instead.

Kāṁbhōji.melakarta: janya of 28 Harikāmbhōji (kākali niṣāda as anya svara)
Kāṁbhōji.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 S
Kāṁbhōji.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Kāṁbhōji.description: Expansive, majestic crowd-favourite; its glowing D2–S curve and rare touch of kakali nishada crown many a concert centrepiece.

Kēdāragauḷa.arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
Kēdāragauḷa.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Kēdāragauḷa.description: Smooth and flowing with an easy grace; shares its skeleton with Surati and Yadukulakambhoji but moves in straighter lines.

Madhyamāvati.arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
Madhyamāvati.avarohana: S N2 P M1 R2 S
Madhyamāvati.description: The auspicious pentatonic that traditionally closes concerts; balanced, serene and instantly settling.

Mukhāri.arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 D2 S
Mukhāri.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
Mukhāri.description: The tradition's great weeping raga — grief and consolation in equal measure, with a dhaivata that darkens on the way down.

Māyāmāḷavagauḷa.arohana: S R1 G3 M1 P D1 N3 S
Māyāmāḷavagauḷa.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M1 G3 R1 S
Māyāmāḷavagauḷa.description: Every student's first scale and a deep raga in its own right; symmetric half-step pairs give it a timeless, temple-like glow.

Mōhanaṁ.arohana: S R2 G3 P D2 S
Mōhanaṁ.avarohana: S D2 P G3 R2 S
Mōhanaṁ.description: The universal major-pentatonic made Carnatic through gamaka; joyous, open-hearted and instantly loved.

Nāṭa.arohana: S R3 G3 M1 P D3 N3 S
Nāṭa.avarohana: S N3 P M1 R3 S
Nāṭa.description: First of the ghana ragas — percussive, bright and ceremonial, powered by its rare shatsruti ri.

Nāṭakurinji.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 N2 D2 N2 S
Nāṭakurinji.avarohana: S N2 D2 M1 G3 M1 P G3 R2 S
Nāṭakurinji.description: A supple, twisting raga that avoids straight lines; its dha-ni play gives it a wistful late-evening colour.

Pūrvīkaḷyāṇi.arohana: S R1 G3 M2 P D2 P S
Pūrvīkaḷyāṇi.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M2 G3 R1 S
Pūrvīkaḷyāṇi.description: Twilight-toned and deeply expressive, pairing a soft ri with Kalyani's bright upper half; a favourite for expansive alapana.

Rītigauḷa.arohana: S G2 R2 G2 M1 N2 D2 M1 N2 N2 S
Rītigauḷa.avarohana: S N2 D2 M1 G2 M1 P M1 G2 R2 S
Rītigauḷa.description: A rich, humid-sounding rakti raga living entirely in curved phrases; its nishada-laden turns are its fingerprint.

Sahānā.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P M1 D2 N2 S
Sahānā.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 M1 R2 G3 R2 S
Sahānā.description: Soft-spoken and pleading, all rounded corners; a raga of intimate appeals rather than grand statements.

Sencuruṭṭi.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
Sencuruṭṭi.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S (phrases characteristically open from the lower D2)
Sencuruṭṭi.description: A breezy, folk-flavoured Harikāmbhōji janya of the concert's final stretch, designed to charm rather than to awe. Its repertoire is jāvaḷis, padams and tukkaḍās rather than kṛtis, so no single composition stands for it.

Sindhubhairavi.arohana: S R1 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S (freely uses all 12 srutis)
Sindhubhairavi.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R1 S
Sindhubhairavi.description: The tradition's most chromatic voice — a tukkada-slot favourite that bends every rule and melts every audience.

Suraṭi.arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
Suraṭi.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 P M1 R2 S
Suraṭi.description: Elegant and understated with a signature curling descent; its ri and ni carry delicate, slippery gamakas.

Sāma.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
Sāma.avarohana: S D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Sāma.description: The raga of tranquillity (shanta rasa) — small in compass, immense in calm.

Sāvēri.arohana: S R1 M1 P D1 S
Sāvēri.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M1 G3 R1 S
Sāvēri.description: Plaintive and deeply traditional; its bare pentatonic ascent blossoming into an ornate descent is pure pathos.

Tōḍi.arohana: S R1 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
Tōḍi.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R1 S
Tōḍi.description: The deepest ocean in the raga system — every note bent and shaded; mastery of Todi is mastery of gamaka itself.

Varāḷi.arohana: S G1 R1 G1 M2 P D1 N3 S
Varāḷi.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M2 G1 R1 S
Varāḷi.description: Ancient ghana raga of eerie, otherworldly intensity — its microtonally low ga and sharp ma create a sound like no other.

Yadukula kāṁbōji.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
Yadukula kāṁbōji.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Yadukula kāṁbōji.description: Unhurried and maternal, with long gliding curves; scale-twin of several ragas yet utterly distinct in gait.

Ānandabhairavi.arohana: S G2 R2 G2 M1 P D2 P S
Ānandabhairavi.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
Ānandabhairavi.description: Sweetly swaying, auspicious raga with borrowed notes worn like jewellery; Śyāmā Śāstri's beloved vehicle.

Śankarābharaṇaṁ.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N3 S
Śankarābharaṇaṁ.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Śankarābharaṇaṁ.description: The Carnatic major scale — vast, luminous and complete; identical to Western major on paper, transformed by gamaka in practice.

Śrī.arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
Śrī.avarohana: S N2 P D2 N2 P M1 R2 G2 R2 S
Śrī.description: Supremely auspicious ghana raga; spare in ascent, ornate in its signature looping descent.

Śrīranjani.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 D2 N2 S
Śrīranjani.avarohana: S N2 D2 M1 G2 R2 S
Śrīranjani.description: Light-footed and charming — the missing pa gives it an airborne, dancing quality.

Ṣanmukhapriya.arohana: S R2 G2 M2 P D1 N2 S
Ṣanmukhapriya.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M2 G2 R2 S
Ṣanmukhapriya.description: Brooding power with a sharpened ma at its heart; a favourite for heavyweight alapanas and tani-avartanam preludes.

Jōnpuri.arohana: S R2 M1 P D1 N2 S
Jōnpuri.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
Jōnpuri.description: A plaintive raga borrowed from Hindustani Jaunpuri — flat dhaivata against a bright rishabha gives it a pleading, devotional color. Limited training data: predictions for this raga are lower-confidence.

Saurāṣtraṁ.arohana: S R1 G3 M1 P M1 D2 N3 S
Saurāṣtraṁ.avarohana: S N3 D2 N2 D2 P M1 G3 R1 S
Saurāṣtraṁ.description: The auspicious mangalam raga that closes most Carnatic concerts; instantly familiar from 'Pavamana Suthudu'. Limited training data: predictions for this raga are lower-confidence.

Hindōḷaṁ.arohana: S G2 M1 D1 N2 S
Hindōḷaṁ.avarohana: S N2 D1 M1 G2 S
Hindōḷaṁ.description: One of the most beloved pentatonic ragas — no rishabha or panchama at all, giving it a floating, meditative gravity. The Hindustani Malkauns is its close cousin.

Abheri.melakarta: janya of 22 Karaharapriya (as commonly sung today)
Abheri.arohana: S G2 M1 P N2 S
Abheri.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
Abheri.description: Pentatonic on the way up, full-scale on the way down — instantly recognizable from Nagumomu. Close to Hindustani Bhimpalasi; older tradition sang it with D1 (Naṭabhairavi janya).

Hamsadhwani.arohana: S R2 G3 P N3 S
Hamsadhwani.avarohana: S N3 P G3 R2 S
Hamsadhwani.description: The classic concert opener — bright, auspicious, and completely without madhyama or dhaivata. Created by Ramaswami Dikshitar; adopted enthusiastically by Hindustani musicians too.

Rēvati.arohana: S R1 M1 P N2 S
Rēvati.avarohana: S N2 P M1 R1 S
Rēvati.description: A modern pentatonic raga with a striking flat rishabha — sparse, spacious, and devotional. Bho Shambho made it a household sound. Hindustani Bairagi is the same scale.

Hamsanandi.arohana: S R1 G3 M2 D2 N3 S
Hamsanandi.avarohana: S N3 D2 M2 G3 R1 S
Hamsanandi.description: Luminous and yearning — prati madhyama and flat rishabha with no panchama anywhere. Essentially Pūrvīkaḷyāṇi without Pa; the model may show both as candidates.

Madhuvanti.arohana: S G2 M2 P N3 S
Madhuvanti.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M2 G2 R2 S
Madhuvanti.description: A romantic mid-20th-century import from Hindustani music — sharp madhyama against a soft gandhara. One swara away from Kalyāṇi (G2 for G3), a distinction the model can miss on short clips.

Kīravāṇi.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N3 S
Kīravāṇi.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
Kīravāṇi.description: The harmonic-minor melakarta — flat dhaivata resolving into a sharp nishada gives it its distinctive ache. A favorite for film scores across Indian languages.

Cārukēśi.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D1 N2 S
Cārukēśi.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G3 R2 S
Cārukēśi.description: Major scale on the bottom, natural minor on top — the turn at dhaivata gives Charukesi its famous bittersweet pivot, beloved of composers and film musicians alike.

Vaḷaji.arohana: S G3 P D2 N2 S
Vaḷaji.avarohana: S N2 D2 P G3 S
Vaḷaji.description: A gliding pentatonic with no rishabha or madhyama — warm gandhara straight to panchama. Popular for varnams and thillanas; Hindustani Kalavati is the same scale. Limited training data.

Śivaranjani.arohana: S R2 G2 P D2 S
Śivaranjani.avarohana: S D2 P G2 R2 S
Śivaranjani.description: Mōhanaṁ with a flattened gāndhāra, one note turning sunshine into melancholy. A Hindustani-leaning raga heard mostly in thillānās, bhajans and film songs rather than in the kṛti repertoire, which is why no single composition stands for it. Limited training data.

Brindāvana Sāranga.melakarta: janya of 22 Karaharapriya (with N3 anya in arohana)
Brindāvana Sāranga.arohana: S R2 M1 P N3 S
Brindāvana Sāranga.avarohana: S N2 P M1 R2 S
Brindāvana Sāranga.description: A monsoon-fresh raga using both nishadas — sharp going up, flat coming down. Rangapura Vihara is its calling card. Kin to Hindustani Brindavani Sarang.

Bauli.arohana: S R1 G3 P D1 S
Bauli.avarohana: S N3 D1 P G3 R1 S
Bauli.description: A dawn raga — pentatonic ascent with flat rishabha and dhaivata, the nishada appearing only on descent. Traditionally sung at daybreak. Limited training data: predictions are lower-confidence.

Ābhōgi.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 D2 S
Ābhōgi.avarohana: S D2 M1 G2 R2 S
Ābhōgi.description: A gentle pentatonic that skips panchama and nishada entirely — warm, introspective, and a favorite for varnams and early-concert kritis.

Śuddha Dhanyāsi.arohana: S G2 M1 P N2 S
Śuddha Dhanyāsi.avarohana: S N2 P M1 G2 S
Śuddha Dhanyāsi.description: Also called Udayaravichandrika — a plaintive pentatonic one flat-third away from Mōhanaṁ's brightness. Close kin of Hindustani Dhani. Limited training data: predictions are lower-confidence.

Amṛtavarṣiṇi.arohana: S G3 M2 P N3 S
Amṛtavarṣiṇi.avarohana: S N3 P M2 G3 S
Amṛtavarṣiṇi.description: The rain raga — legend says Dikshitar sang Anandamrutakarshini and the skies opened. Sharp madhyama against sharp nishada gives it an electric, expectant shimmer. Limited training data.

Nalinakānti.arohana: S G3 R2 M1 P N3 S
Nalinakānti.avarohana: S N3 P M1 G3 R2 S
Nalinakānti.description: A sparkling little raga carried almost single-handedly by one masterpiece — Tyagaraja's Manavyalakincharadate. The zig-zag S G3 R2 opening phrase is its signature. Limited training data.

Kadanakutūhalaṁ.arohana: S R2 M1 D2 N3 G3 P S
Kadanakutūhalaṁ.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Kadanakutūhalaṁ.description: The 'delightful commotion' raga — major-scale notes shuffled into a playful zig-zag ascent. Raghuvamsha Sudha is its brisk, virtuosic calling card. Limited training data.

Vācaspati.arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N2 S
Vācaspati.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M2 G3 R2 S
Vācaspati.description: A Lydian-dominant color — sharp madhyama with a flat nishada. Spacious and slightly wistful; close to Hindustani Yaman with a komal Ni twist. Limited training data.

Śubhapantuvarāḷi.arohana: S R1 G2 M2 P D1 N3 S
Śubhapantuvarāḷi.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M2 G2 R1 S
Śubhapantuvarāḷi.description: The raga of deep pathos — flat rishabha and dhaivata pressed against sharp madhyama and nishada. Carnatic's counterpart to Hindustani Todi (Miyan ki Todi).

Simhēndramadhyamaṁ.arohana: S R2 G2 M2 P D1 N3 S
Simhēndramadhyamaṁ.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M2 G2 R2 S
Simhēndramadhyamaṁ.description: Kīravāṇi's harmonic-minor ache lifted by a sharp madhyama — majestic and intense, a staple of main-piece concert slots.

Chakravākaṁ.arohana: S R1 G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
Chakravākaṁ.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R1 S
Chakravākaṁ.description: Flat rishabha sliding into a bright gandhara — tender and devotional. Hindustani Ahir Bhairav is the same scale, which is why dawn associations cling to it.

Sāramati.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
Sāramati.avarohana: S N2 D1 M1 G2 S
Sāramati.description: Full natural-minor ascent, then a pentatonic glide down that skips panchama and rishabha. Mokshamu Galada — Tyagaraja's meditation on liberation and music itself — defines it. Limited training data.

Darbāri Kānaḍā.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
Darbāri Kānaḍā.avarohana: S D1 N2 P M1 P G2 M1 R2 S (vakra)
Darbāri Kānaḍā.description: Tansen's grand court raga adopted into Carnatic concerts — slow, dignified oscillations on the flat gandhara, sung deep in the lower register. Distinct from the Carnatic Kānaḍa despite the name.

Ranjani.arohana: S R2 G2 M2 D2 S
Ranjani.avarohana: S N3 D2 M2 G2 S R2 S (vakra)
Ranjani.description: A crisp shadava raga — minor gandhara against sharp madhyama, no panchama. Durmargachara, Tyagaraja's rebuke of the corrupt, gives it its stern sparkle. Limited training data.

Bahudāri.arohana: S G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
Bahudāri.avarohana: S N2 P M1 G3 S
Bahudāri.description: Sunny and swinging — the ascent skips rishabha, landing on a bright gandhara. Brova Barama is one of the most beloved short kritis in the repertoire.

Vasantā.arohana: S G3 M1 D2 N3 S
Vasantā.avarohana: S N3 D2 M1 G3 R1 S
Vasantā.description: The spring raga, with no panchama at all and a bright dhaivata against an equally bright gāndhāra. An older tradition places it under 15 Māyāmāḷavagauḷa with the flat dhaivata instead; the recordings collected here favour the Sūryakāntaṁ reading given above. Ancient, auspicious, and tied to festival seasons. Limited training data.

Yamunā Kaḷyāṇi.melakarta: janya of 65 Mēcakaḷyāṇi (bhashanga — uses both madhyamas)
Yamunā Kaḷyāṇi.arohana: S R2 G3 P D2 S
Yamunā Kaḷyāṇi.avarohana: S D2 P M2 G3 M1 G3 R2 S
Yamunā Kaḷyāṇi.description: Kalyāṇi wearing Krishna's smile — the borrowed plain madhyama (M1) melts through phrases like G3-M1-G3. Krishna Nee Begane Baro made it immortal. Hindustani Yaman Kalyan is its twin.

Tilang.arohana: S G3 M1 P N3 S
Tilang.avarohana: S N2 P M1 G3 S
Tilang.description: A light, luminous raga using the sharp niṣāda rising and the flat one falling. Thumri territory in Hindustani music, thillānā and bhajan territory here, which is why no single kṛti stands for it. Limited training data: predictions are lower-confidence.

Desh.arohana: S R2 M1 P N3 S
Desh.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Desh.description: The monsoon-and-motherland raga — Lalgudi's Desh thillana and Vande Mataram both live here. Sharp Ni climbing, flat Ni descending, unmistakably romantic. Limited training data.

Pūrṇacandrika.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 P S
Pūrṇacandrika.avarohana: S N3 P M1 R2 G3 M1 R2 S
Pūrṇacandrika.description: Bright, vakra janya of the major scale. Limited training data.

Maṇirangu.arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
Maṇirangu.avarohana: S N2 P M1 G2 R2 S
Maṇirangu.description: Audava-shadava janya close to Madhyamavati; the G2 in descent distinguishes it. Limited training data.

Pāḍi.arohana: S R1 M1 P N3 S
Pāḍi.avarohana: S N3 P D1 P M1 R1 S
Pāḍi.description: Ancient-sounding raga built on R1 against N3, pentatonic going up and taking a vakra turn through the śuddha dhaivata coming down. That dpmrs phrase is the one everybody names as characteristic. Limited training data.

Kalgaḍa.arohana: S R1 G3 P D1 N1 S
Kalgaḍa.avarohana: S N1 D1 P M1 G3 R1 S
Kalgaḍa.description: Rare vivādi raga known almost entirely through one Syāma Śāstri masterpiece. Printed versions disagree about the madhyama, which some sources omit in name while still notating it in the descent. Limited training data.

Hamīr kaḷyaṇi.arohana: S P M2 P D2 N3 S
Hamīr kaḷyaṇi.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M2 M1 G3 R2 S
Hamīr kaḷyaṇi.description: Kalyani with a plaintive M1 borrowed in descent; Hindustani Kedar's Carnatic cousin. Limited training data.

Kumudakriyā.arohana: S R1 G3 M2 D1 S
Kumudakriyā.avarohana: S N3 D1 M2 G3 R1 S
Kumudakriyā.description: Grave Dīkṣitar-school raga with no panchama at all and the niṣāda appearing only on the way down. Limited training data.

Karṇāṭaka dēvagāndhāri.arohana: S G2 M1 P N2 S
Karṇāṭaka dēvagāndhāri.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
Karṇāṭaka dēvagāndhāri.description: Carnatic equivalent of Bhimpalasi; close to Abheri with its own phrase idiom. Limited training data.

Kuntalavarāḷi.arohana: S M1 P D2 N2 D2 S
Kuntalavarāḷi.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 S
Kuntalavarāḷi.description: Sprightly audava raga that skips Ri and Ga entirely. Limited training data.

Lalita.arohana: S R1 G3 M1 D1 N3 S
Lalita.avarohana: S N3 D1 M1 G3 R1 S
Lalita.description: Serene shadava raga omitting Pa. Limited training data.

Nādanāmakriya.arohana: S R1 G3 M1 P D1 N3
Nādanāmakriya.avarohana: N3 D1 P M1 G3 R1 S
Nādanāmakriya.description: Nishada-bounded raga of quiet pathos; a padam and devotional staple. Limited training data.

Jaganmōhini.arohana: S G3 M1 P N3 S
Jaganmōhini.avarohana: S N3 P M1 G3 R1 S
Jaganmōhini.description: Omits Ri ascending and Dha entirely. Limited training data.

Nīlāṁbari.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 P N3 S
Nīlāṁbari.avarohana: S N3 P M1 G3 R2 S
Nīlāṁbari.description: The lullaby raga; long oscillated G3 and soft N2 touches. Limited training data.

Mārgahindōḷaṁ.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2 S
Mārgahindōḷaṁ.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 S
Mārgahindōḷaṁ.description: Despite the name it is not a form of Hindōḷaṁ: it takes Karaharapriya's full ascent and drops the ṛṣabha coming down. The collected recordings settle it, putting 12 to 19 percent of their pitch mass on a panchama that the Hindōḷaṁ reading does not have at all. Limited training data.

Bāgēśrī.arohana: S G2 M1 D2 N2 S
Bāgēśrī.avarohana: S N2 D2 M1 P M1 G2 R2 S
Bāgēśrī.description: Beloved Hindustani night raga sung in Carnatic concerts as thillanas and bhajans; Pa appears sparingly. Limited training data.

Sāranga.arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N3 S
Sāranga.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M2 R2 G3 M1 R2 S
Sāranga.description: Regal raga with both madhyamas (M1 as a descent grace). Limited training data.

Sālaga bhairavi.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
Sālaga bhairavi.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
Sālaga bhairavi.description: Gentle janya distinguished from Sriranjani and Manirangu by its full descent. Limited training data.

Kēdāraṁ.arohana: S M1 G3 M1 P N3 S
Kēdāraṁ.avarohana: S N3 P M1 G3 R2 S
Kēdāraṁ.description: An auspicious Sankarabharanam janya with no dhaivata and a vakra approach to gandhara through madhyama. The oscillated gandhara is its signature; despite the shared parent scale it never sounds like Sankarabharanam.

Dvijāvanti.arohana: S R2 M1 G3 M1 P D2 S
Dvijāvanti.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 G2 R2 S
Dvijāvanti.description: A Harikambhoji janya adapted from the Hindustani Jaijaivanti. Its signature is the use of BOTH gandharas — the antara G3 on the way up and a brief sadharana G2 on the way down — which gives the raga its characteristic plaintive turn and makes it bhashanga. Rare in concert and associated almost entirely with Dikshitar.

Māṇḍ.arohana: S G3 M1 P D2 S
Māṇḍ.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
Māṇḍ.description: A light, lilting raga of Rajasthani folk origin, absorbed into Hindustani and then into Carnatic concerts as a closing tukkaḍā. The ascent leaves out ṛṣabha and niṣāda, though sources disagree on the exact ascending form. Taken over both directions its note set is exactly Śankarābharaṇaṁ, and what makes it Māṇḍ is the phrasing, the characteristic vakra turns and the wide glides. That is also why note-distribution features cannot tell it apart from its parent: the default model reaches it only through the sequence stage, and the widest model's ensemble carries it outright.

Naṭabhairavi.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
Naṭabhairavi.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
Naṭabhairavi.description: The 20th melakarta and the exact equivalent of the Western natural minor scale. It matters mostly as a parent: Bhairavi, Ānandabhairavi, Hindōḷaṁ, Jōnpuri, Darbāri Kānaḍā and Sāramati are all its janyas. Rarely performed in its own right, and its janyas share its note set, which is why it is one of the hardest classes here.

Śuddha Sāvēri.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
Śuddha Sāvēri.avarohana: S D2 P M1 R2 S
Śuddha Sāvēri.description: A pentatonic (audava) raga dropping both gandhara and nishada from the major scale, leaving a clean, open, majestic frame. Despite its simplicity it is a substantial concert raga. Unrelated to Sāvēri proper despite the name.

Tanarūpi.arohana: S R1 G1 M1 P D3 N3 S
Tanarūpi.avarohana: S N3 D3 P M1 G1 R1 S
Tanarūpi.description: A rarely performed melakarta whose crowded lower tetrachord (R1 and G1 a semitone apart) and very high D3-N3 give it a strained, angular character. Heard almost only in the 72-melakarta cycles.

Nāṭakapriya.arohana: S R1 G2 M1 P D2 N2 S
Nāṭakapriya.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R1 S
Nāṭakapriya.description: A sparsely used melakarta: a low R1 under an otherwise Naṭabhairavi-like upper half, which gives it a plaintive cast. Mostly encountered in melakarta cycles rather than as a concert raga in its own right.

Vakuḷābharaṇaṁ.arohana: S R1 G3 M1 P D1 N2 S
Vakuḷābharaṇaṁ.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G3 R1 S
Vakuḷābharaṇaṁ.description: Māyāmāḷavagauḷa's swaras with the high N3 pulled down to N2, which softens the stern Māyāmāḷavagauḷa colour into something warmer and slightly wistful. Also known as Vasantabhairavi.

Vāgadīśvari.arohana: S R3 G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
Vāgadīśvari.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R3 S
Vāgadīśvari.description: A wide-intervalled melakarta: R3 sits where G2 would, so the ascent leaps early and the raga sounds open and declamatory rather than plaintive.

Latāngi.arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D1 N3 S
Latāngi.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M2 G3 R2 S
Latāngi.description: One of the more popular prati-madhyama melakartas. The sharp M2 against a low D1 gives it a keen, yearning quality, and it takes elaborate alāpana well.

Sucaritra.arohana: S R3 G3 M2 P D1 N1 S
Sucaritra.avarohana: S N1 D1 P M2 G3 R3 S
Sucaritra.description: A rare melakarta pairing a very wide lower tetrachord (R3, G3, M2) with a compressed upper one (D1, N1 a semitone apart), so the two halves pull in opposite directions.

Rasikapriya.arohana: S R3 G3 M2 P D3 N3 S
Rasikapriya.avarohana: S N3 D3 P M2 G3 R3 S
Rasikapriya.description: The last of the 72 melakartas, and the most stretched: every variable swara takes its highest form, so the scale is almost all wide intervals with tight pairs at the top of each tetrachord.

Gaṁbhīra nāṭa.arohana: S G3 M1 P N3 S
Gaṁbhīra nāṭa.avarohana: S N3 P M1 G3 S
Gaṁbhīra nāṭa.description: Nāṭa with R and D dropped, leaving a five-note scale that is symmetric in both directions. Bright, ceremonial and firmly weighted, and often used to open a concert or a temple performance.

Janaranjani.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 P N3 S
Janaranjani.avarohana: S D2 P M1 R2 S
Janaranjani.description: Śankarābharaṇaṁ whose ascent curls back through the panchama before reaching the niṣāda, and whose descent drops both gāndhāra and niṣāda. The two directions therefore sound quite different while drawing on exactly the parent's swaras, so it is separated from Śankarābharaṇaṁ by phrasing rather than by scale.

Mandāri.arohana: S R1 G3 M2 P N3 S
Mandāri.avarohana: S N3 P M2 G3 R1 S
Mandāri.description: Kāmavardani (Pantuvarāḷi) with the dhaivata dropped in both directions. The R1 against M2 and N3 makes it sound taut and bright, quite unlike its heavier parent.

Puṇṇāgavarāḷi.arohana: N2 S R1 G2 M1 P D1 N2
Puṇṇāgavarāḷi.avarohana: N2 D1 P M1 G2 R1 S N2
Puṇṇāgavarāḷi.description: A niṣādāntya raga: its range runs from N to N rather than S to S, so phrases settle on the niṣāda instead of the tonic. Long associated with lullabies, folk melody and snake-charmer music, and sung plainly with far less gamaka than Tōḍi, whose seven swaras it shares exactly.

Cittaranjani.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2
Cittaranjani.avarohana: N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
Cittaranjani.description: A niṣādāntya raga: it stops at the niṣāda and never reaches the upper ṣaḍja, which is its one structural feature. Otherwise it takes exactly Karaharapriya's seven swaras, so its identity rests on characteristic phrases and nothing in the notes themselves separates it from the parent.
